title: Who Carries a Creative Vision Into Production?
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: Creative vision reaches production through negotiated translations among people, factories, contractors, files, budgets, standards, law, and material limits; the process distributes power rather than merely executing a designer’s command.
A garment record becomes institutional evidence when material, date, maker, identifier, and rights remain attached.

01 · TRANSLATE — What does “the vision” mean operationally?. Turn aesthetic direction into testable specifications while preserving the reason behind them: material, construction, tolerance, finish, movement, color, hand, durability, repair, packaging, cost, timing, and acceptable variation.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · LOCATE LABOR — Who performs each transformation?. Name the actual employer, worker, contractor, vendor, or licensee where verified; record jurisdiction, role, classification source, wage-and-hour review, safety route, language access, and subcontracting uncertainty. Do not let a purchase order erase people.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · ALLOCATE POWER — Who can approve, reject, revise, pause, and be paid?. Bind decisions to thresholds, response times, evidence, escalation, payment milestones, change-order treatment, quality disputes, intellectual-property terms, confidentiality, and termination. “Final approval” must name both subject and consequence.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · CLOSE THE LOOP — What returns from production to the house?. Capture deviations, defects, worker or supplier feedback, material substitutions, fit outcomes, quantities, waste, cost changes, approvals, corrected specifications, provenance, and archive records so production knowledge can alter the next collection.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

mapping.prompt: Trace one style from approved concept through every entity, location, file, sample, shipment, and approval to final receipt.
Identify every place where subcontracting, classification, pay, safety, or decision authority is unknown.
Compare the written specification with the production outcome and record each deviation and who absorbed its cost.
Interview participants separately about where the process lost information or shifted risk, then preserve disagreement rather than averaging it away.
